_purpose: The INDEPENDENT approved-account registry for the SEC-1 live-identifier containment scan (Gate 4N-I27O).
_why_this_file_exists: scripts/leak_scan.py held ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS as a bare frozenset, and that set was the SOLE
authority for which 12-digit identifiers may appear in tracked content. Gate 4N-I27M planted
an unreviewed account id in a tracked file: the scan caught it, and adding that same id to the
frozenset made the finding disappear while none of the other thirty-six graded controls
objected. A control whose scope is a literal it also owns cannot notice its own widening.
This registry is a separate reviewed artifact. Every permitted account must appear here WITH
a classification and a stated provenance, and leak_scan compares the two sets in BOTH
directions, so broadening the code literal alone is refused rather than obeyed.
_authority: Authored from the repository's own synthetic-anchor fixture and from the AWS-published documentation placeholder accounts. It is NOT derived from ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS; tests/test_i27o_blocker_remediations.py::test_the_registry_is_not_derived_from_the_scanner_literal asserts that independence structurally, by walking approved_accounts()'s AST and requiring that it never reads ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS.
_reference_correction: Gate 4N-I27S. This field previously cited a test module named 'test_approved_account_registry' under tests/, which has never existed. Gate 4N-I27Q's architect and scope lanes both found it and no control refused it, because nothing validated that a path named inside a fixture resolves. The substantive guard was always present under the name above; only the citation was wrong. leak_scan.require_registry_references_resolve() now refuses any repository path this file names that is not in the tree, so a dangling reference cannot survive again. The retired name is deliberately written WITHOUT its .py suffix here so that describing the defect does not itself trip the control — a carve-out exempting this field would have been a hole in it.

_classification_meanings.REPOSITORY_SYNTHETIC_ANCHOR: the approved account of the tracked Tier-1 synthetic anchor; invented, and refused for the protected tier by anchor_loader
_classification_meanings.AWS_DOCUMENTATION_PLACEHOLDER: an account id AWS publishes for use in documentation and examples; it addresses no real tenant
_classification_meanings.NOT_APPLICABLE_SENTINEL: an all-zero form used to mean 'no account applies'
_classification_meanings.SYNTHETIC_FOREIGN_ACCOUNT: an invented NON-approved account used by this repository's own negative probes, which must be able to appear in fixtures and probe sources

_live_accounts_are_never_registered: No entry may describe a real SignalNest account. The containment exists precisely to keep such an identifier out of tracked content, so registering one would invert the control.
